sentence: Prednisolone is a steroid, or corticosteroid, medicine.
note: NHS About page summary: a steroid or corticosteroid medicine.

sentence: It is used to reduce swelling (inflammation), and it can calm the immune system.
note: NHS: treats swelling (inflammation) and can calm down the immune system.

sentence: It is available only on prescription, as tablets or as a liquid that is swallowed.
note: NHS About page: prescription only, tablets and liquid you swallow.

sentence: The NHS says a doctor may still recommend it for people with conditions such as diabetes, high blood pressure, or heart, liver or kidney problems, if they think the benefits outweigh the risks.
note: NHS Who can take it: doctor may recommend if benefits outweigh risks in these conditions.

sentence: Steroid tablets are not usually recommended for children because they can cause growth problems.
note: NHS: not usually recommended for children as they can cause growth problems.

sentence: The NHS says prednisolone tablets or liquid are best taken once a day in the morning, so the medicine does not keep a person awake.
note: NHS How to take: once a day in the morning so it does not keep you awake.

sentence: Taking it with food lowers the chance of stomach problems.
note: NHS: take with food to reduce the chances of stomach problems.

sentence: The NHS lists problems sleeping, weight gain and indigestion as the most common side effects.
note: NHS side effects page: most common are problems sleeping, weight gain, indigestion.

sentence: Long-term use can cause thinner bones (osteoporosis), poorly controlled diabetes, eyesight problems and high blood pressure.
note: NHS: long-term use can cause thinner bones, poorly controlled diabetes, eyesight problems, high blood pressure.

sentence: Serious side effects are more likely with a higher dose or after taking prednisolone for more than a few weeks.
note: NHS: more likely with higher dose or longer use; sources vary slightly on duration so no figure given.

sentence: Signs of infection, such as a high temperature, a very sore throat, ear or sinus pain, a cough, or mouth sores or wounds that will not heal, need a call to a doctor or NHS 111 straight away.
note: NHS: call a doctor or 111 for signs of infection (list as in search summary).

sentence: The NHS gives the same route for signs of high blood sugar, Cushing's syndrome, adrenal problems or low potassium, and for eyesight changes, unusual bruising or bleeding, and red or black poo.
note: NHS list of call-a-doctor-or-111 signs (from search summary).

sentence: Mood changes such as depression or confusion can happen, and the NHS says the higher the dose, the more intense they can be.
note: NHS: mood changes; higher dose, more intense.

sentence: For thoughts of self-harm or ending life, the NHS advises asking someone to drive to A&E or calling 999 for an ambulance, rather than driving alone.
note: NHS: ask someone to drive you or call 999; do not drive yourself.

sentence: Sudden swelling of the lips, mouth, throat or tongue, or fast or difficult breathing, can be a serious allergic reaction and needs a 999 call.
note: NHS: call 999 for swelling of lips, mouth, throat or tongue / signs of serious allergic reaction.

sentence: The NHS says people who take prednisolone for a longer period, or at a high dose, are given a blue steroid treatment card.
note: Search summary of NHS: blue steroid card given for longer or high-dose courses.

sentence: A steroid emergency card is also carried by people who take prednisolone for adrenal conditions such as Addison's disease or congenital adrenal hyperplasia, or for other adrenal, hypothalamic or pituitary problems.
note: NHS: steroid emergency card for Addison's, CAH, adrenal insufficiency, hypothalamic or pituitary disorder.

sentence: NHS guidance warns against stopping prednisolone suddenly after long use or at high doses, because this can cause withdrawal side effects.
note: NHS: do not stop suddenly after long courses or high doses; thresholds omitted.

sentence: Stopping suddenly can make the adrenal glands stop working properly, with extreme tiredness, nausea, dizziness and loss of appetite.
note: NHS: adrenal gland stops working; symptoms extreme tiredness, nausea, dizziness, loss of appetite.

sentence: Adrenal problems are among the signs for which the NHS advises calling a doctor or NHS 111.
note: NHS side effects list: adrenal problems, call doctor or 111.

sentence: Steroid sick-day guidance from one NHS trust says that vomiting with tablets that cannot be kept down needs a 999 call straight away.
note: NNUH sick day rules: if vomiting and cannot keep steroid tablets down, call 999 immediately.

sentence: The NHS advises telling the doctor about any infection, such as COVID-19, and about contact with infectious illnesses like chickenpox, shingles or measles.
note: NHS 111 Wales steroid tablets: tell your doctor if you get an infection or are exposed to chickenpox, shingles, measles.

sentence: People on prednisolone are advised to avoid close contact with anyone who has measles, chickenpox or shingles.
note: NHS 111 Wales: avoid close contact with people who are ill, especially measles, chickenpox, shingles.

sentence: If exposure may have happened, the advice is to get medical advice as soon as possible.
note: NHS 111 Wales: get medical advice as soon as possible; retrieved text did not name a specific service.

sentence: The NHS advises telling the doctor about all other medicines before starting steroid tablets, including herbal remedies and supplements.
note: NHS 111 Wales: tell doctor about other medicines, herbal remedies, supplements.

sentence: Alcohol is usually allowed in small amounts, but too much may irritate the stomach.
note: NHS 111 Wales: can usually drink alcohol but not too much as it may irritate your stomach.

sentence: Liquorice is best avoided because it can increase the amount of prednisolone in the body.
note: NHS 111 Wales: do not eat liquorice; increases amount of medicine in body.

sentence: The NHS says to tell the doctor before treatment starts if pregnant, breastfeeding or trying for a baby.
note: NHS: tell doctor if pregnant, breastfeeding or trying for a baby.

sentence: A very small amount of prednisolone can pass into breast milk, and the NHS says this has not been shown to cause problems for babies at the doses it discusses.
note: NHS breastfeeding text; dose threshold deliberately omitted.
